prompt:
I need the front end for Tallyway. A free personal money app with tens of millions of users that links people's bank and card accounts and lets them find any past charge by describing it in plain words.

Who's using it: Renée, a 34-year-old dental hygienist who uses the app a couple of times a month, mostly to check her balance. She isn't comfortable with finance jargon and finds bank merchant codes baffling.

What they're doing right now: She just noticed her checking balance is $90 lower than she expected and suspects a free trial she signed up for in the spring turned into a paid subscription. She types something like 'that yoga or fitness app from March' and needs to find the charge, see whether it's recurring and how much she's paid in total, and decide whether to cancel it. While she's looking, the app has also picked up other charges that look like forgotten subscriptions, and she wants to go through them and flag the ones she doesn't recognize.

What's in the system at this point: Two linked accounts: Harbor Federal checking (••4471) and a Cobalt Rewards Visa (••0938), with 14 months of history and about 1,920 transactions. Merchant descriptors are messy, e.g. 'SQ *FLOWSTATE YOGA 8774', 'APPLE.COM/BILL 866-712', 'PAYPAL *STRMNGSVC', 'AMZN Mktp US*2K4L19'. Matching candidates: FlowState Yoga $14.99 monthly since April 2 (8 charges, $119.92 total), an Apple.com/bill charge of $12.99 on the same dates, and a one-time $29 Peloton-like charge from March 11. Possible forgotten subscriptions the app has found: a cloud photo plan at $2.99 per month, a meal-kit service skipped for 5 weeks then charged $71.94 last week, a newspaper digital edition at $1 that rose to $17 in September, and two streaming services both billing on the 15th. Each charge has a date, amount, account, cleaned-up merchant name, category and recurrence pattern.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
